newsitem.title: UK: Healthy N.Sea July sales push Brent spreads firmer.
newsitem.headline: Healthy N.Sea July sales push Brent spreads firmer.

text.p: Recent brisk sales of July-loading North Sea cargoes helped push the July/August Brent spread to the brink of backwardation on Monday.
The front spread was talked at -4 cents to flat in late discussion, having traded at a high of -6 cents and a low of -11 cents earlier.
A rush of buying on Friday saw over seven million barrels of the July loading programme change hands.
"Last week we saw some stronger numbers and some healthy selling, but this week looks even better balanced from a seller's point of view," said one trader.
But the wet market was fairly quiet on Monday with two Ekofisks, loading July 22-24 and July 25-27 heard traded at Dated Brent +21 cents and +25 cents respectively.

A U.S. refiner was heard offering a Brent at August Brent -20 cents, with bids at -25 cents. CFDs for next week were traded at August -29 cents and -25 cents, with later weeks in slight backwardation.
No Brent cargoes were nominated from the paper chains on Monday.
The August/September Brent spread also gained ground, talking late at -11/-7 cents, having traded at -13 cents, with heavy maintenance expected to hit North Sea loadings in August.

A Reuters survey of field operators showed some 7.6 million barrels, an average of 245,000 barrels per day, will be lost to the work against July production. That sum equates to a shortfall of around 15 standard 500,000 barrel cargoes from the August loading programme.

Outright August Brent was trading 18 cents up at $18.36 a barrel at 1758 GMT, having reached a high of $18.45 on the back of comments from Iraqi envoy Abdul Amir al-Anbari on Saturday saying he didn't expect a resumption of Iraqi exports until August.
